description.narrative:
"The EC and the WB share a common vision of building competitive and sustainable economies and in reducing poverty and social exclusion. These goals are outlined in the EU's Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) (2014-2020) - ""The EU as a global player"" and in the proposed MFF for 2021-2027 – “Neighbourhood and the World”. The MFFs are designed to allow the Union to fulfil its responsibility both at global level and in its immediate neighborhood, and to help safeguard global public goods, i.e., fighting poverty and promoting democracy, peace, stability, and prosperity.
The MFF 2014-2020 supports the EC’s approach under the ""Agenda for Change"", to focus EU aid in fewer sectors supporting, inter alia, good governance and creating inclusive and sustainable growth. In the context of the establishment of the Part III – EEPP program, it is important to take into account the new MFF which has been presented by the EC on May 2, 2018. In fact, the program will ideally coincide with the timeframe of the current and next proposed MFF for 2021-2027. The latter will be guided by the EU’s new consensus for development, which aims to foster sustainable development by focusing on cross-cutting elements of development policy such as gender equality, youth, investment and trade, sustainable energy and climate action, good governance, democracy, rule of law and human rights, and migration and mobility.
A continued constrained growth and a tight fiscal environment in the Neighborhood, Western Balkans, Turkey, and Central Asia make it important for the EC and the WB to coordinate policy advice, where appropriate, and to allocate their resources in the region in the most strategic and effective way possible. As a result, the EC and the WB have begun since 2011 to interact more directly by means of a programmatic TF to support the Europe 2020 Agenda, which has allowed the WB to engage directly with individual European countries on projects that are financed by the governments entirely or in part by EU External Action Instruments and other EU resources, such as the Structural Funds, the Rural Development Fund or the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA).
1.2. Areas of joint cooperation and the World Bank advisory activities envisioned under the Program
The EC and the WB agree that more direct interaction would be beneficial to both institutions and through them to the countries. This applies particularly to the provision of analytical, advisory and knowledge services, capacity and institution building, and technical assistance, but also to projects executed by respective governments. The EC has demonstrated its interest in specific analytical projects to be carried out by the WB which provides guidance for investments in the long-term prosperity and stability of the EU's neighborhood and support the reform process in those countries preparing for EU membership.
Areas of common interest are regularly discussed and refined on the occasion of sub-regional country day meetings between the services of the EC and WB that are held on an annual basis and reviewed by means of an annual High-Level Dialogue with DG NEAR. These meetings have focused on the Eastern Neighborhood, Central Asia and Pre-Accession countries, and on the developmental challenges faced in the Region and which require a shared vision, coordinated efforts and complementarity of actions. For the current MFF 2014-2020 the instruments offered by the EC, and that the WB can help implement are: Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA), the European Neighborhood Instrument (ENI), the Development Cooperation Instrument (DCI), the Partnership Instrument (PI), and Macro-Financial Assistance (MFA). For the next MFF 2021-2027, the relevant instruments will be the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NDICI - 22 billion for ECA Countries) and the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA III – 14.5 billion).
As part of the EC - World Bank Partnership Programme Part III for Europe and Central Asia Programmatic Single-Donor Trust Fund - Fergana Valley Water Resources Management Project Phase II Activities and in line with the new European Consensus on Development, the European Commission has expressed an interest in ensuring that the Bank provides support to Uzbekistan in the framework of the Trust Fund with the specific objective to improve the quality of irrigation and drainage service delivery to agricultural users and boost diversification of sustainable high productive agriculture within the Project area"
